rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation is the prescribed signature in `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.node_id`: `impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> { pub fn node_id(&self) -> &NodeId<D>; }`. It requires a public method that takes `&self` and returns a borrowed `&NodeId<D>`, which is the identity of the node being checked. Returning an owned or cloned `NodeId` would not satisfy it. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#1/fn[node_id]` declares exactly `pub fn node_id(&self) -> &NodeId<D>` and returns `&self.node`. It borrows the stored node identity and has the {impl} marker for this requirement. No other root or delegation is needed, because the method is a direct accessor.

behavioral: The only obligation is that `ValidationContext::node_id` borrows the identity of the source node being checked. The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[labeled_selections_track_only_target_membership_without_reading_contents]` builds a context with `ValidationContext::new(&graph, intern_node(1))` and asserts `ctx.node_id() == &intern_node(1)`. The assertion compares against the constructed subject node. The test also uses other nodes as edge targets (9, 7, 5 and so on), so an implementation that returned an edge target instead of the subject would fail. The `&NodeId` comparison checks the borrowed return. I did not use the public-API test `public_exports_match_the_appendix` as evidence for this obligation. The requirement has no failure cases or boundaries beyond this, so I found no gap.
